newsitem.title: UK: British gun laws among toughest in Europe.
newsitem.headline: British gun laws among toughest in Europe.

text.p: Britain has probably the toughest gun laws in Europe after its announcement on Wednesday of an almost total ban on handguns following the massacre of 16 children and their teacher at Dunblane, Scotland, in March.

The government proposed passing legislation in the next session of parliament to ban all hand guns of more than .22 inch calibre. It said remaining handguns, used for target shooting, would have to be kept under lock and key at licensed gun clubs.
The following is a list of gun laws in selected European countries:
AUSTRIA - Anyone may apply for a licence who is over 21, has no criminal record, no history of psychological problems and who can satisfy the Interior Ministry they need a gun.
DENMARK - Special interest must be proven, for example membership of hunting or shooting club. Medical certificates and doctors' statements are required and anyone with a criminal record is excluded.

FINLAND - Hunting tradition means one Finn in five owns a shotgun. Licences are granted only to those of "reliable character" with an "acceptable reason". A special permit from provincial authorities is needed for non-hunting weapons.
FRANCE - Authorisation is granted after a police inquiry and excludes anyone with a criminal record. The overwhelming majority of permits are granted to hunters.

GERMANY - Purchaser of a gun must prove that he/she is a hunter with licence, or a member of a rifle or shooting club. A tiny number of people (for example politicians and top industrialists) are allowed to keep guns for protection.
GREECE - Private ownership of handguns or rifles are not permitted. Shotguns for hunting are allowed.

ITALY - Five types of gun licence are issued. They must be obtained from police station before purchasing weapons and include permits for handguns and rifles for self-defence and shotguns for hunting.
NETHERLANDS - Guns are outlawed for most citizens except army and police. Exceptions are those who can prove a reasonable interest, such as members of shooting clubs and hunters.
